record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: Reports a runtime projection ablation using per-layer difference-in-means directions and measures refusal and other behaviors. This tests the causal claim conceptually, but does not use the original single-direction intervention unchanged.
record.gate_note: The README reports measured outcomes for a per-layer runtime ablation. Its direction-cosine measurements also bear on the single-direction versus multiple-directions question. Harvest timing, byte audits, speed estimates, and cited results from other work are not rows because they do not report outcomes of the claim's refusal behavior or direction intervention.
record.test_reason: The study applies a difference-in-means projection ablation at runtime on GLM-5.3-Flash. It uses per-layer directions with a strength λ, a variant of the original's single direction. It reports refusal rates on held-out sensitive and benign prompts, plus capability checks at each λ. These results bear directly on V1's claim that ablation removes refusal while keeping other abilities.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say the per-layer runtime ablation roughly halves refusals (75% to about 35–40%) while benign refusals, comprehension and tool calling are preserved. The refusal curve is U-shaped: it rises again at λ=2.0, and the model collapses by λ=2.5, where 0% refusal is an artifact. No λ reaches 0% refusal with the model functional. With 24 prompts (SE about 10pp), the drop from 75% is resolved but the fine structure is not. They frame the work as a measurement of the method's limits and costs.
record.recipe_differences: Per-layer difference-in-means directions are subtracted from the residual at runtime, rather than testing one shared direction. This is a measurement/tool repository, not a stated reproduction of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal changes non-monotonically with λ: it falls through λ=1.5, rises at λ=1.75 and 2.0, then the model collapses at λ=2.5. The README says the λ=1.0 versus λ=1.5 difference is not resolved by the 24-prompt sample.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-layer DIM refusal directions in GLM-5.3-Flash have cosine to the mean direction of min 0.093, median 0.527, max 0.600 (200 pairs). The result is stable at 40 pairs. Direction norm peaks in late layers (‖d‖ 18.59 at layer 44).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The difference-in-means refusal direction rotates substantially across depth, so one vector captures only part of it in some models.

record.problems: One model and one machine are reported. The refusal evaluation uses 24 held-out prompts; the README estimates standard error near 0.4 at about 10 percentage points and says fine differences are unresolved. The capability checks are limited to 6 comprehension cases, a prose output, and 12 tool-calling cases. The zero-refusal result at λ=2.5 is confounded by empty output and model collapse.

untested.parts: Not tested: adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; one shared direction applied at all layers, as in the original; any model other than GLM-5.3-Flash. Capability checks are small: 6 comprehension cases, 1 prose sample, 12 tool cases.
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction structure within a layer. The cross-layer rotation measured (R32–R33) is a different question.

record.verdict_notes: The source is the README only; code and raw JSON were not read. The reader's 'challenges' label for V1 was changed to limits_scope, because refusal clearly drops (partial), not absent or reversed. The V4 'supports' label was removed: cross-layer rotation is not V4's within-layer multi-direction claim, and no behavioural comparison was made. The method differs from the original (per-layer directions, λ-scaled projection, hyperconnection mean space). Partial removal may therefore reflect the variant rather than V1 itself. Single model, single machine, small samples.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests. Uses per-layer directions rather than one direction applied at every layer and position. Tests only one model and a small held-out set.
No weight edit is evaluated for refusal behavior; the runtime hook leaves weights unchanged.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is evaluated.
Measures per-layer direction geometry, but does not test affine or cone models, or compare those alternatives behaviorally.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is evaluated.
No variation in refusal training method or timing is evaluated.

tranche.reason: This is difference-in-means projection ablation, but with per-layer directions and a strength λ at runtime instead of one shared direction. It measures refusal on held-out sensitive prompts, so it is a different method aimed at the same question.

source_check.notes: Text is the README only, and it was read in full. The model is turboderp's GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 2.05bpw quant. The README does not say how refusals are scored or how many benign prompts there are, and it reports no random-direction control, so controls=y overstates. The authors say 33.3% and 41.7% are not resolved (n=24, SE about 10pp); only the 75% to about 40% drop is outside noise. The per-layer vs mean-direction cosines (median 0.527) are descriptive: no single-direction ablation is run for comparison.
